source: Whether an emulated rotary identifies itself to software as a rotary (diode D23 fitted). Most rotary controllers ever built shipped without the diode and identify as a standard joypad, which is the default here. Tempest 2000 does not read this -- it uses its own CONTROLLER TYPE menu instead.

Tempest 2000 does not read this -- it uses its own CONTROLLER TYPE menu instead.

source: Standard Joypad (no diode -- as most real units)
effective_source: Standard Joypad (no diode -- as most real units)

source: Discards spinner movement at or below this many host units per poll. A noise gate for a jittery source; movement above the threshold passes at full size.
effective_source: Discards spinner movement at or below this many host units per poll. A noise gate for a jittery source; movement above the threshold passes at full size.

source: Subtracts a constant from every spinner sample. Cancels a source that reports a small non-zero movement while at rest, which would otherwise spin the knob forever with the controls untouched. Applied in host orientation, before the wheel's direction convention.
effective_source: Subtracts a constant from every spinner sample. Cancels a source that reports a small non-zero movement while at rest, which would otherwise spin the knob forever with the controls untouched. Applied in host orientation, before the wheel's direction convention.

source: Response exponent for the spinner, giving finer control at low speed. The curve is anchored at 64 units per poll: below that an exponent above 1.00 attenuates, at and above it movement passes through unchanged. A higher exponent therefore makes the spinner SLOWER overall -- raise Rotary Sensitivity to get the top speed back.
effective_source: Response exponent for the spinner, giving finer control at low speed. The curve is anchored at 64 units per poll: below that an exponent above 1.00 attenuates, at and above it movement passes through unchanged. A higher exponent therefore makes the spinner SLOWER overall -- raise Rotary Sensitivity to get the top speed back.

source: Stick positions within this many ADC counts of centre (127 = full deflection) read as exactly centred. The rest of the travel is rescaled so the response is smooth at the edge and full deflection still reads full scale.
effective_source: Stick positions within this many ADC counts of centre (127 = full deflection) read as exactly centred. The rest of the travel is rescaled so the response is smooth at the edge and full deflection still reads full scale.

source: As Analog Controller Dead Zone (X), for the Y axis (pitch, or accelerator/brake on the driving controller).
effective_source: As Analog Controller Dead Zone (X), for the Y axis (pitch, or accelerator/brake on the driving controller).

source: Subtracts a constant (in ADC counts) from every X sample, in host orientation before any device convention. Cancels a stick that rests off-centre; a centred stick is moved by it, which is the point.
effective_source: Subtracts a constant (in ADC counts) from every X sample, in host orientation before any device convention. Cancels a stick that rests off-centre; a centred stick is moved by it, which is the point.

source: As Analog Controller Offset (X), for the Y axis.
effective_source: As Analog Controller Offset (X), for the Y axis.

source: Response exponent for the X axis, anchored at full deflection: an exponent above 1.00 gives finer control near centre while full deflection still reads full scale. Unlike the mouse/rotary curves this costs no top speed, so there is no paired sensitivity control.
effective_source: Response exponent for the X axis, anchored at full deflection: an exponent above 1.00 gives finer control near centre while full deflection still reads full scale. Unlike the mouse/rotary curves this costs no top speed, so there is no paired sensitivity control.

source: As Analog Controller Response Curve (X), for the Y axis.
effective_source: As Analog Controller Response Curve (X), for the Y axis.

source: Map Jaguar numpad 0-9, * and # to keyboard keys. 'Number Row Keys' will use 1234567890-= keys, 'Keypad Keys' will use 0123456789/* keypad keys.
effective_source: Map Jaguar numpad 0-9, * and # to keyboard keys. 'Number Row Keys' will use 1234567890-= keys, 'Keypad Keys' will use 0123456789/* keypad keys.
